title: Bill microbatches by request provenance for mixed KV/prefix cache hits
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When multiple incoming requests are merged into a single microbatch by the serving runtime, the batch can contain heterogeneous cache outcomes: some requests hit the prefix cache, some have partial KV cache hits, and others are cold. Current metering attributes whole-batch token charges or applies coarse prorating that produces unfair quota usage and odd rate-limit behavior (thundering small tenants charged for others' cold tokens, or customers seeing spiky quota drains). This ticket proposes a provenance-based metering model for merged microbatches to precisely attribute token charges and quota decrements to originating requests based on their execution cost share and cache hit semantics.
background: We already have several metering rules for cache/coalesced batches (see ENG-7429, ENG-40211). However those approaches either: 1) bill the entire merged batch to the owner of the largest request, 2) prorate simply by token count ignoring cache-related savings, or 3) treat prefix cache hits differently but only at microbatch granularity. None of these handle mixed KV+prefix hits within the same GPU pass where some tokens are skipped due to KV hits while others are generated. This causes two customer-visible problems: billing accuracy degradation (invoices don't match token counts expected by customers) and quota/rate-limit anomalies (unexpected early throttling or delayed throttling).
proposal: Introduce a light-weight per-request provenance vector that travels through batching and execution stages. At batch assembly time, record for each request: (a) requested max_tokens, (b) observed prefix KV hit mask (if known), (c) prefetch reservation tags (reserved vs speculative), and (d) origin tenant/account. During execution, collect an execution-cost vector describing per-token compute/time cost contributions (coarse-grained: cold token compute weight, KV-hit token weight=near-zero, prefix-hit weight=small). After the GPU step completes, run an attribution pass: compute each request's share of total compute-weight and token-forwarded. Charge token billing by actual output tokens but prorate the GPU compute and quota consumption by the computed weight share. Rate limiting must decrement from each origin's bucket by their attributed quota share immediately (no eventual reconciliation required).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Accuracy: For a synthetic workload with three requests merged (one full KV-hit, one 50% KV/prefix partial hit, one cold), billing lines reflect: output tokens charged to request owners; GPU compute cost prorated according to compute-weight within 2% of ground truth simulation.
2) Quota behavior: Tenant quotas are decremented at request completion by attributed quota amount; no customer sees >10% deviation vs simulated expected quota when varying hit rates.

3) Rate-limiter compatibility: Attribution logic integrates with existing token-bucket rate limiter such that cross-tenant microbatching does not increase observed latency for any request by more than 5ms on average.
4) Backwards compatibility: Default config preserves current billing semantics when provenance is disabled; feature flag rollout path exists.
5) Logging/trace: Each billed event contains provenance metadata (request_ids, computed_weights) for audit and debugging.
implementation_plan: Design phase (1): Define provenance vector schema (request_id, tenant_id, max_tokens, prefetch_tag, observed_cache_mask) and compute-weight heuristics (cold=1.0, prefix_hit=0.2, kv_hit=0.05) — Diego/Applied ML to validate weights.

Runtime hooks (2): Add lightweight provenance header to requests entering the batching queue; ensure propagation through batch coalescer and kernel scheduler — change surface in runtime/queue (low risk).
Execution telemetry (3): Emit per-batch execution measurements (wall-time, tokens_generated, kv-skipped-count) from the GPU host side and attach to provenance vector in memory before deallocation.

Attribution pass (4): Implement an attribution module that consumes batch-level telemetry + provenance vectors to produce per-request billing records and quota decrements. Add to metering pipeline (near the cost-aggregation step).
Billing pipeline (5): Extend invoicing events to include provenance fields; update analytics jobs to accept provenance-aware rows for downstream display and cost breakdowns.
Feature flag + rollout (6): Gate attribution behind 'provenance_metering' runtime flag; start with internal beta on dedicated pools, then opt-in tenants, then global default.
Docs & SDKs (7): Document semantics and examples in billing docs; SDK returns 'metering_provenance' in the response metadata when enabled.
PRs & code review (8): Keep changes small per repo: runtime queue, gpu-host telemetry, metering service adapter, billing events.
testing_plan: Unit tests: provenance vector serialization, weight calculations, attribution math under edge cases (all kv hits, all cold, zero-output).
Integration: end-to-end test where we generate mix of requests, execute on a test runtime, and assert billing/exported CSV lines match expected attribution model.
Load test: run microbatch-heavy synthetic workload at scale to verify rate-limiter interaction — ensure latency SLOs preserved.
Audit test: export logs for 1000 merged batches and run offline reconciler to compare per-request charges between legacy and provenance models.
Customer simulation: replay a sampled week of production traces with provenance metering enabled to estimate invoicing delta and quota deltas by tenant tier.
observability: Emit metrics: provenance_batches_total, provenance_attr_error_count, provenance_avg_compute_weight_ratio, provenance_latency_overhead_ms. Traces include tags: provenance_enabled:true/false, batch_id, batch_size. Add dashboard panels to billing-sli dashboard.
risks: Computation overhead: attribution pass adds CPU work — mitigate by keeping vector small and batching attribution per N batches.
Billing surprises: customers may see invoice changes vs previous coarse heuristics; mitigate by opt-in beta and clear changelog + sample simulation tool.
Edge-case fairness: exact prorating heuristic may be disputed — provide configurable weights and a reconciliation job to adjust retrospective invoices in extreme cases.

Rate-limiter integration: immediate quota decrements require low-latency attribution; if attribution stalls, we risk inconsistent throttling. Plan to fallback to conservative upfront deduction (estimate) and reconcile post-facto.
